A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExIde business-rule extraction work. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, prompts, and appendices support comparison despite substantial benchmark and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 LLMs in Tables 4–6, annotation-quality measurements, and experimental case studies.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs in Tables 2–4, dependency-type and complexity analyses in Figures 3–4, annotation-quality measurements, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: The two-stage extraction/dependency procedure and five prompting strategies remain. However, Prompt 4's demonstration changes from grouping b, c, and d into one equality rule in v1 Figure 11 to separate equality rules in v3 Figure 13, changing the extraction guidance. Pseudo-code prompting already existed in v1; its renaming as executable grounding is not a new component.

E1.justification: BPRF becomes BREX with substantially broader represented domains. Beyond v1's banking, healthcare, e-commerce, manufacturing, and service examples, v3 Section 3.2 explicitly includes scientific research management, administrative approvals, legal processes, and financial compliance across over 30 domains. The rule-extraction and dependency-identification tasks remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated model roster is largely replaced across all three tasks. v1's GPT-4o/o1, ERNIE, ChatGLM/GLM, Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5, QwQ, and DeepSeek-v3 comparisons give way to Gemini-2.5, GPT-5, Kimi-k2, DeepSeek-3.1/3.2-exp, and Qwen3 variants. DeepSeek-R1 remains. These changes appear in the actual result tables, not merely the references.

E3.justification: The evaluation corpus expands from 50 documents/326 rules to 409 documents/2,855 rules, and synthetic generation changes from ChatGPT-3.5 to Gemini-2.5-Pro. v3 adds rule-count and rule-pair-count stratification and evaluates the stricter atomic equality convention. Agreement assessment changes from annotating the dataset to an unspecified subset. v1 specifies Macro-F1 for classification; v3 says only F1, leaving any averaging change unresolved.

E4.justification: v3 adds dependency-type comparisons and systematic analyses of extraction performance versus rule density and dependency performance versus pair count (Figures 3–4). Appendix A.7 replaces v1's flight-booking, foreign-currency-deposit, and DeepSeek shopping analyses with leave, credit-card, and fixed-deposit cases examining equality over-merging and pseudo-code-induced spurious rules.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 4 introduces error bars and accompanying discussion of variability, whereas v1 provides point estimates and case scores without such dispersion displays. The bars' statistical meaning and calculation are unspecified. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or significance tests; ICC and Fleiss' Kappa remain the annotation-agreement measures.

E6.justification: The experimental results are substantially replaced. v1 Tables 4–5 report P1 as best on average for NER (0.910) and P4 for logical classification (0.5947); v3 Tables 2–3 favor P5 (0.882 and 0.850). These are different corpora/model rosters, not same-setting performance changes. Dependency results, complexity findings, and case outcomes are also replaced or added. Reported ICC changes from 0.904 to 0.892 and Kappa from 0.911 to 0.901.

T1.justification: v3 explicitly normalizes complex conditions into atomic rules and specifies that equality operates on a single value (Appendices A.1 and A.7). This revises the semantics illustrated by grouped equality values in v1 Table 8 and Figure 11. The condition–action schema and dependency categories otherwise remain; added graph notation largely formalizes existing content, and no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate executable grounding's superiority to a central empirical contribution; v1 instead emphasizes general framework effectiveness and finds different prompts best for different extraction components. v3 also claims substantially broader regulatory coverage and emphasizes deployment without fine-tuning and recovery of long-range, non-linear dependencies.

C2.justification: v3 replaces much of the prompt interpretation with arguments about pseudo-code as a structural scaffold, equality over-merging, and abstraction-induced precision loss. It adds qualifications about P4 outperforming P5 in some dense cases. Limitations now explicitly cover quadratic pairwise scaling and omitted temporal constraints, exceptions, and probabilistic rules, while the earlier small-dataset limitation is removed.

D1.justification: v1 promises dataset release after acceptance; v3 states that both code and data are available and supplies a repository link, materially changing reported resource access. Appendices A.5–A.6 add text-quality criteria and annotation-processing explanations, and Figure 14 supplies the pseudo-code example's input. Conversely, v3 drops the explicit Macro-F1 specification. Resource availability is reported by the PDF and was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds a systematic comparison of eight existing benchmarks by size, modeling paradigm, and source (Appendix A.4, Table 6). It expands positioning against synthetic procedural datasets and schema-constrained instruction tuning, adding works including PET, ProcessTBench, and Pyrih et al. (2025). This goes beyond v1's narrative action-flow versus rule-flow distinction; the benchmark comparison is not an experimental baseline evaluation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the Logic Gap and executable grounding. BPRF and prompt terminology are renamed, methodology and experiments gain dedicated subsections, and definitions move into an appendix expanded into A.1–A.7. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The dataset-construction and framework diagrams are redrawn, performance tables gain color shading, and the dependency table changes from a wide horizontal display to a vertical model list. New radar and complexity plots are added. Dataset statistics and annotation illustrations move to the appendix, case tables are replaced, and the earlier DeepSeek output/reasoning figures are removed. The three dependency-example diagrams are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the limited empirical basis acknowledged in v1: broader regulatory coverage, matched Instruct/Thinking comparisons, systematic complexity tests, and concrete failure analyses make the findings more informative than aggregate scores and selected success cases alone. Clearer annotation guidance and reported code/data access also improve usefulness. Important weaknesses remain: error bars are undefined, and P5's small average leads in Tables 2–3 lack significance testing, limiting the stronger superiority claims.
